statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 10% with NQ mid-range of its overnight band after the push to the 31,411.25 Globex high was retraced.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON. The 13:00-15:00 UTC window spanning the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech is the session's main checkpoint, and the published forecast reaches WATCH there. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds mid-range overnight after retracing its Globex high, leaving mean reversion intact below a record cash close
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,358.50, up 40.75 points (+0.13%) from the 31,317.75 previous close, having retraced the advance to the 31,411.25 Globex high. Price now sits 49.25 points above the 31,309.25 overnight low and 52.75 below that high, almost exactly mid-range of a 102.00-point band worth about 0.33% of index value. That two-sided profile is the decisive observation: the overnight push was given back and then partially rebought rather than extended, which is working mean reversion and not the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score is built to detect. The pattern is corroborated across risk assets. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,834.50 (+0.11%) are confined to a 9.50-point range, and the Nikkei 225 at 70,081.53 (+0.19%) is mid-range of 69,813.16-70,416.78, cooling after Monday's advance rather than driving futures onward. The higher-timeframe backdrop is genuinely bullish: the cash index closed on 5 October at a record 31,076.44, up 268.51 points (+0.87%), with a record intraday high of 31,117.36, while the Nasdaq Composite added 1.05% to its own record 27,477.31 and Nvidia closed at $238.90, up 2.12%. Under the operating contract that regime is context for conditional risk, not current structure, because no persistent directional efficiency is observable in the overnight tape. The standing tension is the bond market: the 10-year yield rose 3.40 basis points to 5.3110% and the 30-year 3.45 basis points to 5.6645%, while the 2-year eased 1.07 basis points to 4.8143%, a bear steepening driven by the September ISM services reading of 54.9, which slowed from 55.4 but retained elevated price pressures. Equities at records advancing against long-end yields near multi-decade highs is a cross-asset conflict rather than an alignment, and a conflict of that kind raises Stress and tempers conviction rather than mechanically raising Tail. Volatility stays contained with VIX at 15.52, and energy is firm but easing, with November WTI having settled at $89.43 (-1.84%) and December Brent at $100.32 (-1.89%) before WTI steadied at $89.75 overnight; Brent above $100 reflects the continuing Middle East shipping backdrop and is a persistent Stress input with no new escalation identified overnight. Against that evidence Tail is 10%, Stress 45% on compressed realised volatility offset by yield and energy pressure, and Confidence 86% on fresh verified futures, index, volatility, yield, energy and calendar evidence. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September and is reported partial, so it fails the 90-minute freshness test and was excluded; the independent research above carries this assessment instead.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band apart from the 19:00 UTC hour, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance to a record close. Tail ran from 10% in the Asian session on 5 October down to 6% by 08:00 UTC, climbed through the European and U.S. sessions to that 20% peak at 19:00 UTC, then decayed to 9% by 00:00 UTC, printed 12% at 01:00 UTC on a new Globex high and eased back to 9% at 02:00 UTC. Stress fell steadily from 57% to 45% as realised volatility compressed even while long-end yields stayed near multi-decade highs, and Confidence held between 86% and 89% throughout. The 06:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail holds near 9-10% through the thin late-Asian and pre-European hours, steps up from the European cash open at 08:00 UTC, peaks at 20% across the first two U.S. cash hours, then decays through the afternoon with a secondary 17% reading in the power hour before easing to 10% by the Asian session on 7 October. Stress tracks the same shape between 43% and 55%. Confidence declines from 86% to 78% across the window as distance from the verified overnight price evidence grows. Every hour beyond the current clock hour is conditional: no European or U.S. price path has been observed at assessment time, and the scheduled items in the event calendar are checkpoints rather than assertions about outcomes. The FOMC minutes and the 10-year auction fall on 7 October after this window closes.
